chunks: Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn Mahbub narrated from 'Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Sulayman, who said:

I wrote to the jurist, Abi al-Hasan al-'Askari عليه السلام, asking him about one who has fallen unconscious for a day or more: should he make up what he missed of the salat (prayer), or not? So he wrote عليه السلام: He does not make up the sawm (fasting), nor does he make up the salat (prayer).

key_terms.الْفَقِيهِ: the jurist; here, a title used for the Imam عليه السلام
key_terms.يَقْضِي: to make up a missed religious obligation

ai.seo_question: Does an unconscious person have to make up missed prayers and fasting in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith records a written question to Imam Abi al-Hasan al-'Askari عليه السلام regarding the ruling for a person who was unconscious for a day or more. The Imam عليه السلام replies that such a person does not make up the missed sawm (fasting) or salat (prayer), indicating a legal ruling related to acts of worship missed during unconsciousness.
